executive_assessment.text: Balochistan's policy identifies gendered health-access and rural livelihood barriers, while WHO supplies a dated monsoon response with named service locations.
IPC adds Kachi/Tank livelihood and market constraints from insecurity, with separate drought-related survey findings and limited rural-district coverage.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy says declining groundwater, recurring drought and heatwaves erode agriculture and displace vulnerable, resource-dependent rural communities, increasing poverty in Balochistan.

Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy reports that rain-induced floods displaced over 1.3 million people in Balochistan in 2022; women, youth and vulnerable communities face disproportionate climate-related food and health risks.
Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy says climate disasters combined with social norms obstruct women's access to healthcare, including transport, supplies, skilled staff and information.

Source dated 2025-07-25 reports: As of 25 July 2025, NDMA reported 266 deaths and 628 injuries from heavy rain and flash floods since 26 June; reported deaths included 144 in Punjab, 63 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 25 in Sindh and 16 in Balochistan.

Source dated 2025-07-25 reports: By 25 July 2025, health contingency plans and high-risk district control rooms were activated, medical supplies prepositioned, and partner mobile units had served over 3,000 people in Rawalpindi, Chakwal, Attock, Sargodha, Sohbatpur and Usta Muhammad.
IPC's February 2026 analysis classified food insecurity for December 2025–March 2026 across 45 rural districts, citing weather shocks and localized insecurity among several drivers.
Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: IPC identifies localized insecurity as a main food-insecurity driver in Kachi and Tank, disrupting livelihoods, markets, services and income.

Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: The household assessment associated drought with income declines of 30% in Balochistan, 14% in Sindh and 9% in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; respondents also reported water scarcity and reduced crop or livestock production.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 16 of 16 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The 2021 NDC is a dated national synthesis; updated province-level climate and food-security indicators were not checked.
The PDNA is a rapid post-disaster assessment based on data collected September to mid-October 2022; it warns that inaccessible areas and time constraints limit accuracy.
The PDNA reports flood impacts but does not establish climate-change attribution for the 2022 event.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

The accessed sources establish climate-related displacement, health and livelihood vulnerability, and localized insecurity as a separate food-insecurity driver; they do not establish that climate hazards caused armed conflict.
Balochistan policy findings are provincial and do not quantify district differences; WHO's July 2025 report is an early operational snapshot, not a final impact assessment.
IPC findings refer to its December 2025–March 2026 assessment period and cover 45 rural districts, fewer than its prior analysis; they are not current October 2026 estimates.
UNHCR's original Forced Displacement Survey PDF returned HTTP 429 and its alternate mirror timed out; no claims were taken from search snippets or the opened publisher summary.
Do not infer a climate-to-conflict chain from the overlap of food insecurity, drought/floods and insecurity. Localized Kachi/Tank conflict constraints are independently identified.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
